findings.title: Preserve per-key synchronization while building indexes
findings.description:
Moving the cache lock to only the final assignment allows `GetIndex` to return a cache miss while an index for that same key is already being built. In `resource/search.go`, both search requests and write-event handling use the unsynchronized `getOrCreateIndex` check-and-build sequence.

Consequently, concurrent requests can build separate indexes for the same key. A write event can update one completed index before another build overwrites its cache entry, leaving searches using an index without that update. Disk-backed builds can also compete to create the same directory.

Keep builds for different keys parallel, but serialize or single-flight the complete lookup/build/publication operation for each key. Add a concurrent search/write regression test that verifies updates remain searchable.

findings.title: New startup document count can race with index publication
findings.description:
The new `TotalDocs()` call occurs after the event-consumer goroutine starts. An event for a resource not indexed during initialization can therefore build and publish another index concurrently with this call.

`bleveBackend.TotalDocs` in `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:144-153` iterates `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`, while `BuildIndex` writes to that map under the mutex. This is an unsafe concurrent map iteration/write and can terminate the process. The existing metrics collector also calls this method, so moving the log before the goroutine would not fully address the synchronization defect.

Protect `TotalDocs` with the corresponding read lock, or copy the cached index pointers under that lock before counting. Cover concurrent building and counting with a race-detector test.

findings.title: PostgreSQL integration coverage is disabled rather than repaired
findings.description:
The unconditional PostgreSQL skip removes coverage of storage-server startup and instrumentation on a supported backend, including local environments where the comment says the test works. This is particularly relevant because this change moves database initialization and watcher startup into `NewResourceServer`.

Repair the CI-specific configuration or startup synchronization instead of disabling the backend entirely. If temporary quarantine is necessary, narrowly scope it to the affected environment and link a tracked issue with a clear removal condition.
